messages:
Maria Chen: quick share — ran a microprofile against nightly serving on ampere, saw a ~12% p99 latency regression for short sequences (<=32) when continuous-batching is enabled. forwarding full traces below. :thinking:

Kevin Patel: hmm, did the kernel selector flip to a different GEMM path under that seqlen? sometimes the autotuner picks the packed-kernel for mid-lengths and launch overhead spikes for tiny batches.

Maria Chen: @Kevin I dug in — yes. profiler shows path switch at seqlen 24. at runtime the scheduler sometimes groups a 4x batch of seqlen 16 and switches to the tiled kernel that has higher kernel-launch overhead. trace snippet:
```
[2026-03-10T15:02:11Z] batch_start id=0 size=4 seq=16 kernel_hint=packed_tile
[2026-03-10T15:02:11Z] launch kernel=packed_tile launch_us=45 exec_us=120 total_us=170
[2026-03-10T15:02:11Z] batch_start id=1 size=1 seq=512 kernel_hint=kv-friendly
[2026-03-10T15:02:11Z] launch kernel=kv_fused launch_us=8 exec_us=450 total_us=458
```
Maria Chen: net effect is increased tail because those small batches pay an extra ~40us launch cost repeatedly. also noticed KV cache hits change the seq distribution mid-query when clients do streaming concat — that pushes timeline into a different kernel path.

Sachin Rao: interesting — so it's not just batch size but the sequence-length distribution over time. continuous batching mixes requests with different effective seqlens and the kernel selector is reacting per-batch rather than per-epoch. that oscillation could cause thrashing between kernels. :eyes: 

Liam Ortiz: can you paste the autotuner thresholds? we have heuristics: if mean_seq <= 64 -> low-latency kernel, else high-throughput. but we also have an arch override for A100 vs A800. maybe the arch-aware pick is shadowing the seqlen rule.

Maria Chen: here's the relevant config from the canary cluster:
```
autotune:
  rules:
    - name: small_seq
      cond: mean_seq <= 32
      kernel: small_launch_opt
    - name: mid_seq
      cond: 32 < mean_seq <= 256
      kernel: packed_tile
    - arch_overrides:
      ampere: prefer_packed_tile: true
```

Kevin Patel: two quick ideas: 1) use sequence-length histograms instead of mean — median/90p avoids a single outlier flipping the rule; 2) add a lightweight cost-model that includes expected launch_us * batch_count + exec_us * tokens. then pick kernel minimizing expected total_us.

Sachin Rao: +1 on cost model. also suggest hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping: require a sustained window (e.g., 500ms) or N consecutive batches before switching the kernel path. that reduces thrash.

Maria Chen: i tried a small experiment switching to median-based rule locally. p99 improved by ~9% for the workload with streaming KV hits. but throughput slightly down for long sequences (as expected).

Liam Ortiz: is the KV cache behavior predictable? if streaming clients append tokens gradually, prefix caching means early batches = short seqlens, later batches = long. scheduler could route by request-phase (prefetch phase vs steady phase) if we detect streaming sessions.

Kevin Patel: also check launch overlap: if we can pipeline kernel launches (stream-based), we can hide some launch_us. but that depends on kernel compatibility and memory layout. worth measuring.

Maria Chen: logged a perf regression ticket with traces and experiment results: https://internal/rdw/infra/PR-8742 (canary id: canary-2026-03-10-09). planning an A/B roll where we enable: median-based pick + 500ms hysteresis + per-arch cost-model.

Sachin Rao: add seqlen histogram to the sampling telemetry and a per-route flag to opt out (for critical latency routes). will add a lightweight recorder today.

infra-bot: experiment deployed to canary-2026-03-10-09 for route /v1/generate (token-limit=1024). experiment id=exp-5221.

Maria Chen: sweet, thanks. next steps: collect 24h of telemetry, then decide on default heuristic. if anyone has quick microbench ideas to stress the kernel-switch boundary on A800 please drop them here. :thumbsup:

Kevin Patel: I'll run synthetic mix (50% seq=16, 50% seq=512) across batch sizes [1,2,4,8] on both A100/A800 and post numbers.

Liam Ortiz: i'll add the hysteresis patch and a flag to the autotuner to enable/disable arch overrides so we can test both behaviors without a deploy rollback.

Maria Chen: awesome — ping me the dashboards when ready. thanks all! :rocket:
